problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Eigenvectors of a 3x3 Matrix With Distinct Eigenvalues

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvectors of a 3x3 Matrix
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069621/assets/1503285c91d0c320a3720c702b620bfe2156ed713d915b04c22bd35c06a05cd8.png)

The vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1=1$ and $\lambda_2=-1$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector $\mathbf{v}_3=\big[ a, \, b, \, c \big]^T$ such that the set $\{ \mathbf{v}_1,\mathbf{v}_2, \mathbf{v}_3 \}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\dfrac{a}{c}?$
examples.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is a diagonal matrix, we have that its eigenvalues are the entries in the main diagonal, that is, $\lambda_1=1,$ $\lambda_2=-1$ and $\lambda_3=4.$ 

Also, since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors $\{ \mathbf{v}_1,\mathbf{v}_2, \mathbf{v}_3 \},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ correspond to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1=1$ and $\lambda_2=-1.$ Thus, the third eigenvector $\mathbf{v}_3$ must correspond to $\lambda_3=4.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =4.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}=0 \\ -5{x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the augmented matrix $M$ is already in its row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In this matrix, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, $x_3$ is a free variable. From the first and second equations, we obtain $x_1=x_2=0.$  Therefore, the general solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069621/assets/7aab21fae627c5fe36b144f4a1e12a2d5e57ef7c2c987fbee64f718c7cbb7404.png)

Setting, for instance, $x_3=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069621/assets/c080641a794b7a65f7893429d32920f39bfb4d87d9193197afd6b48dacc697a3.png)

Finally, $\dfrac{a}{c}=\dfrac{0}{1}=0.$

feedback.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-5{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-(\frac{1}{4}){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{2}:=(\frac{1}{4}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\  & ={x}_{2}+2(0) \\  & ={x}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
